name: period-jitter-band-top
description: closed-loop deterministic period jitter at the 200 MHz TOP of the ratified output band: the same control-ripple-driven period-to-period spacing sim/period-jitter measures at 150 MHz, moved to the band edge that binds (#13). f_ref and the Icp trim code are held; N goes 6 -> 8 and the VCO band code becomes per-corner, because spec/pll.md's band-selection rule selects band 6 at 34 of the 45 PVT points and band 7 at the other 11
claim: spec/pll.md#period-jitter -- period jitter (RMS), percent of output period, in lock, at the 200 MHz end of spec/pll.md#output-band. DETERMINISTIC component only (control-line ripple); random/noise-driven jitter is not measured by this record -- see Methodology.
methodology: WHY THIS CAMPAIGN EXISTS. sim/period-jitter (#13) measures the deterministic, control-ripple-driven period jitter of the locked output -- but every record it has is at ONE output frequency, 150 MHz, band 6, N = 6. spec/pll.md#output-band ratifies 10-200 MHz, and 200 MHz is the end that binds: it is where sim/reference-spur's two coldest corners already land over the -55 dBc spur line once scaled, it is where the band-selection rule forces the loop onto its highest-Kvco configurations, and a fixed absolute jitter is a larger PERCENTAGE of a shorter period, which is the form spec/pll.md#period-jitter states its target in. Nothing in this repository bounded closed-loop period jitter there before this campaign.

WHY A SIBLING CAMPAIGN RATHER THAN A SECOND GRID INSIDE sim/period-jitter. The manifest-level `checks` that decide whether a point is locked -- `fout` inside its band, `nmeas` at the configured N -- are per manifest, not per point (sim/harness/README.md), and this operating point has a different N (8 rather than 6) and a different output band. Widening those checks to span both frequencies would weaken the lock gate at BOTH, which is the one thing that must not be weakened: a period sequence read off an unlocked loop is not jitter. Same reasoning that makes sim/divider-ratio-{cell,chain,dff} siblings rather than one manifest.

WHAT CHANGES FROM sim/period-jitter, AND WHAT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT. Changed, and only these three: f_out 150 -> 200 MHz; N 6 -> 8; band code 6-everywhere -> per corner. Held identical so the difference is attributable to the frequency and not to the setup: f_ref = 25 MHz (so the per-reference-cycle ripple mechanism is excited at the same rate -- only the ring it modulates has changed); Icp trim code 0, one unit leg, which is not a convenience but what spec/pll.md's Icp trim-code rule REQUIRES at f_ref = 25 MHz, and holding f_ref is precisely what lets this campaign hold the trim code; ideal 4x-unit-leg bias sources, as in every closed-loop campaign here; the same .tran controls, lock baseline and measurement window, which at 200 MHz is 400 output cycles rather than 300; and the same reduction code, loaded from sim/period-jitter/testbench/derive.py rather than copied, so the two campaigns' numbers are comparable by construction.

THE BAND CODE IS NOT A FREE CHOICE, AND AT 200 MHz IT IS NOT CONSTANT. spec/pll.md's band-selection rule (normative, DR-003 Decision 4) requires the LOWEST 3-bit band code that reaches the target frequency; it is normative because Kvco is proportional to f_osc WITHIN a band, so a higher code reaching the same frequency does so near the bottom of its own Vctrl range where its Kvco is already large -- 154.3 MHz/V under adversarial band choice, past DR-001's ~150 MHz/V fixed-filter bound, against 115.8 MHz/V under the rule. Applied to sim/vco-tuning-range's committed f(Vctrl) record (20260804-162735-72883fb) at 200 MHz, the rule selects band 6 at 34 of the 45 PVT points and band 7 at the other 11 -- the cold and/or high-supply points where band 6's own curve tops out below 200 MHz. At 150 MHz one static code covers all 45, which is exactly why sim/reference-spur and sim/period-jitter could hold it fixed; at 200 MHz none does. That is a finding this campaign records, not a difficulty it works around: configuring one convenient static band across the whole grid would be measuring a MIS-CONFIGURED part at some corners, and spec/pll.md says plainly that no row of the specification applies to such a part. band_and_vstart_from_vco_record.py in this directory derives all 45 (band, vstart) pairs from the committed record and the ratified rule, re-checks the manifest against them (--check) and regenerates the manifest fragment from them (--emit); check_config.sh diffs every static bit, including each point's band bits, against sim/lib/pll_top_dut.sh's own encoding.

WHAT THE BAND SPLIT DOES TO THE LOOP, STATED IN ADVANCE OF THE MEASUREMENT. Local Kvco at the selected operating point ranges 74.7-117.0 MHz/V across the 45 points (all inside spec/pll.md row 17's 150 MHz/V bound), against 74.1-78.2 MHz/V for sim/period-jitter's five 27 C/3.30 V points at 150 MHz. The loop gain A = Icp*Kvco/N that this fixed passive filter sees therefore varies by about 1.6x across this campaign's own grid where sim/period-jitter's varies by about 1.05x. This is a PREDICTION of what the grid will look like, derived from a committed open-loop record; it is written here so that it can be checked against the closed-loop numbers this campaign actually measures, not offered in place of them.

WHAT IS MEASURED. Identical to sim/period-jitter: once locked, the PFD fires both branches once per reference cycle for the reset-delay overlap, the charge pump's per-event charge asymmetry lands on the loop filter's C2, and the resulting Vctrl ripple phase-modulates the ring. sim/reference-spur reads that ripple out of the output SPECTRUM as a sideband; this deck reads the identical physical ripple out of the output's TIME-DOMAIN edge sequence, which is the form spec/pll.md#period-jitter states its target in (percent of period, RMS) rather than dBc.

MEASUREMENT CRITERION: the reported RMS/pp period jitter and TIE come from every rising mid-supply crossing of v(clk) in the measurement window (`wa` to `wb`, 2.0 us = 400 output cycles at 200 MHz), linearly interpolated between the two straddling ngspice timepoints (sim/vco-tuning-range's `_numeric.py:crossings`). Period jitter is the RMS/pp deviation of the per-cycle period sequence from its own mean; TIE is the RMS/pp deviation of the crossing times from their own least-squares line, which keeps residual settling drift out of the jitter number. sim/tests/test_period_jitter_derive.py replays a synthetic waveform of known jitter through this exact reduction path, off any simulator -- and covers this campaign because derive.py here IS that file, loaded rather than copied.

STEADY STATE, NOT LOCK TIME. Each point is released at its own predicted lock point in its own selected band, for the same reason sim/period-jitter does it: the loop's slow closed-loop pole is 1/(R*C1) = 9.3 us, so a common release voltage would spend tens of microseconds slewing at Icp/C1 = 14 mV/us before any measurement window could open. The residual settling drift this leaves is not assumed away -- `ferr` is measured over a 1 us baseline (`ta`/`tb`) immediately before the measurement window and gates the point, and `tie_*` de-trends the crossing sequence by its own least-squares line.

THE LOCK GATE IS WRAP-SAFE, AND IS CORROBORATED BY A WRAP-FREE SECOND MEASURE (#273). Identical to sim/period-jitter, whose manifest carries the full derivation. `phi_a`/`phi_b` are `trig`/`targ` edge-pair delays and are therefore each wrapped into one reference period, so their difference is unwrapped into (-T_ref/2, +T_ref/2] before it is divided by the baseline -- `dphi = (phi_b-phi_a) - (1/fref)*floor((phi_b-phi_a)*fref + 0.5)`, `ferr = -dphi/(tb-ta)` -- and the residual aliasing blind spot at multiples of T_ref/(tb-ta) = 0.04 is closed by `ferr_fb = ffb/fref - 1`, a period-count frequency error with no wrap at all, checked at +-2e-3. The `ferr` gate itself is unchanged at +-1e-3: this is a wrap fix, not a loosened tolerance. Note that this campaign divides by 8, not 6, so its `ferr`/`ferr_fb` are still referred to the 25 MHz reference, not to the 200 MHz output.

RANDOM / NOISE-DRIVEN JITTER IS NOT MEASURED BY THIS RECORD -- the same disclosed methodology gap sim/period-jitter states in full. DR-002 Decision 5 ratifies (status: proposed) a VCO-dominated transient-noise testbench plus a jitter-transfer argument as the intended method; this repo's pinned ngspice-46 injects no automatic device noise into a .tran, and turning ngspice's explicit trnoise() PWL source into a credible device-noise-equivalent figure needs a noise-PSD calibration this repository has not done. No random/noise-driven period-jitter number appears anywhere in this record.

SIMULATOR SETTINGS. `.tran 2n 5.7u 3.5u 100p` -- the fourth argument is the 100 ps ceiling on ngspice's INTERNAL timestep every campaign whose DUT contains the PFD inherits (sim/README.md, 'Closed-loop internal-timestep bound'), verified per point via `dt_int_mean`. At 200 MHz that ceiling is also exactly 1/(50*f_out), so it bounds the output edge sequence at 50 points per period as well as bounding the PFD. `.option rshunt=1e12 itl4=200 reltol=1e-3 abstol=1e-13 vntol=1e-6` matches sim/period-jitter's and sim/reference-spur's exactly, so this deck's converged solution is comparable with theirs.

LIMITATIONS. (1) Random/noise-driven jitter is not measured -- see above. (2) Schematic-level: no layout parasitics, no supply or substrate coupling into the VCO rail beyond what design/pll_top.sch itself models. (3) The reference is ideal: no reference jitter, no duty-cycle error. (4) Device mismatch is OFF (no Monte Carlo). (5) One (f_ref, N, trim) operating point at one output frequency -- the top of the band; sim/period-jitter holds the 150 MHz middle, and no record of either campaign covers the 10 MHz floor. (6) The release voltage is an ESTIMATE interpolated from a committed OPEN-LOOP f(Vctrl) table, not a per-corner closed-loop solve; where it missed far enough to leave the loop unlocked the point fails this manifest's ferr/fout/nmeas checks and is reported as a failing point rather than as jitter. (7) Whatever subset of the declared 45-point grid a given record ran is stated in that record's Corner matrix field -- read it before citing this campaign's coverage.

jitter.description: the measurement this record exists for -- the deterministic period/TIE jitter of the locked output at the 200 MHz top of the band

lock.description: is the loop actually locked -- a period sequence from an unlocked loop is not jitter

integration.description: the standing guards: the PFD's DN branch must assert at all, and the internal timestep ceiling must actually be in force

op.description: the per-PVT-point operating point: the VCO band code the band-selection rule selects for 200.0000 MHz at that corner, and the control-node release voltage at which that band's committed f(Vctrl) curve (record 20260804-162735-72883fb) reaches it. band_and_vstart_from_vco_record.py in this directory recomputes all 45 from that record and the ratified rule, and diffs them against this manifest. The band code is a real static configuration input of the part, so getting it wrong would mean measuring a mis-configured part; the release voltage only sets where the loop STARTS, and a point whose estimate missed far enough to leave the loop unlocked fails this manifest's ferr/fout/nmeas checks rather than being reported as jitter.
